page: Amazon Web Services c7a.large is a compute-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz without hyperthreading. System memory consists of 4.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a standard compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage and zero discrete GPUs, relying on network-attached storage volumes for file systems and data persistence. Network connectivity provides a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-core performance alongside capacity limits inherent to a dual-core allocation. The c7a.large achieves top-quartile results in single-threaded tests, including stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core evaluations, aided by support for advanced vector extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16. Single-threaded decompression benchmarks also score in the upper quartile. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads, including aggregate compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and parallel PassMark tests, fall into lower performance tiers due to the low total core count. Memory bandwidth scores remain modest, reflecting the entry-level memory configuration.

From an efficiency perspective, the instance offers dedicated high-frequency physical cores at an entry-level tier, avoiding the resource contention common to burstable or shared-core alternatives. The primary tradeoffs involve the modest 4.0 GB memory envelope and reliance on remote block storage, which constrain data-heavy or memory-intensive tasks. The c7a.large is best suited for workloads requiring reliable single-thread compute rather than extensive parallelization, such as lightweight web application servers, small build and continuous integration agents, microservices, and dedicated monitoring or utility tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 2 dedicated physical CPU cores clocked at 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 4.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz. The instance includes no local storage or discrete graphics hardware, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data, and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmark profiles highlight strong single-threaded throughput, evidenced by top-quartile results in Geekbench single-core and stress-ng tests, supported by hardware AVX-512 vector extensions. However, its modest two-core footprint limits aggregate multi-threaded capacity and memory bandwidth relative to larger instances. The instance delivers cost-effective dedicated compute capability for entry-level workloads that prioritize clock speed over memory volume, such as lightweight web services, small batch processing, single-threaded compression utilities, and dedicated CI/CD execution nodes.
